name: Micromobility Device
description: A motorized transportation device for individual use, typically 20 to 36 inches wide and 50 pounds or less, that operates typically under 15 mph and never faster than 28 mph; the term spans bicycles, electric bicycles and motorized scooters, privately owned or shared. A light electric bike outside the e-bike classes that tops out at 28 mph can fit it. Defined by Florida Statutes §316.003(41) as rewritten by chapter 2025-149 (SB 462, 2025) and regulated by §316.2128.

restrictions.rule: Designed for individual use, typically 20 to 36 inches wide and 50 pounds or less; those figures are typical, not hard limits
Operates typically under 15 mph and can't exceed 28 mph
No driver's license, registration or insurance required
Has a bicycle rider's rights and duties, and is exempt from the ban on motorized vehicles on sidewalks and bicycle paths
A local government may regulate it on streets, highways, sidewalks and sidewalk areas
Since July 1, 2025 a local government may set minimum ages by ordinance and require riders to carry government-issued photo ID
Before July 1, 2025 the term covered only app-rented shared-fleet devices capped at 20 mph
